projectBriefConcise: Single Storey Rear Extension creating an enlarged Kitchen and a new Dining Room, Internal Alterations to the existing Lounge and Dining Room, and refurbishment of the First Floor Bathroom and En-Suite.
projectBriefFull:
## Project Overview And Goals

The primary aim is to create considerably more living space and a much larger, more sociable kitchen. The existing kitchen lacks usable food preparation space, and the worktop provision is modest for a house of this size, so a significant increase in preparation space is one of the defining goals of the project.

The new accommodation is intended for everyday family living and for hosting, with a noticeably better flow between the kitchen, dining and living spaces when guests are in the house.


## Proposed Ground Floor Alterations

A single storey extension will be added to the rear of the property, extending back to the point at which the current patio ends.

The central section of the new extension will house the enlarged Kitchen. The hob and cooker will remain on their existing wall, which was confirmed as an important requirement during the site visit, and that wall will continue to form the cooking wall in the new layout.

A new Island will be introduced into the enlarged room. This addresses the current shortage of food preparation space and also provides a social seating area, with breakfast stools to one side, creating a kitchen that is properly fit for entertaining.

The wing of the extension adjacent to the existing Bay Window will extend the current Lounge outwards to form a new Dining Room.

Internally, the wall in the centre of the current Lounge which separates the existing small Dining Room from the Lounge will either be removed or substantially widened. The current intention is to introduce internal glazed sliding doors in this position, which can be opened to create a single large space or closed to separate the two rooms. The resulting space will become the main Living Room.

Subject to what can be comfortably accommodated, there may also be scope for a casual seating and television area within the extension itself. This will be tested as the layout develops.

In massing terms, the extension is arranged as two linked sections. A pitched, tiled roof section feeds onto a lower break front section which steps forward towards the garden, giving the rear elevation depth and articulation rather than presenting as a single flat run across the back of the house. An early mock-up of this arrangement was prepared and discussed on site during the initial visit.


## Proposed First Floor Alterations

One Bathroom and the En-Suite require updating. Whether this is delivered as a complete replanning of the layouts, or as new fixtures, fittings and finishes within the existing layouts, is still to be decided and will be agreed at the next meeting on site.


## Design Style And Key Features

The preferred architectural language is a mix of traditional and modern, rather than something strongly contemporary. The existing Bay Window is to be retained, and the intention is that one half of the building remains visually unchanged.

An appreciation has been expressed for the character of David Salisbury and Vale orangeries and conservatories, which gives a useful steer on the glazing, proportion and detailing of the new rear elevation. The intention is to develop the extension as a Vale garden house style structure, with generous, finely divided glazing and a strong glazed gable to the break front section.

The pitched section will be finished in roof tiles selected to sit comfortably against the existing clay tiled roof, and the lower section is proposed to carry a roof lantern to bring light deep into the centre of the new Kitchen. This approach allows the new work to read as a considered addition in keeping with the character of the existing house, whilst still delivering the light and openness the brief calls for.

A change of Roof Tiles to the existing property is also included within the scope.


## Key Constraints

The Local Planning Authority is Nottingham City Council.

It is not yet established whether the works will proceed under Permitted Development or via a Householder Planning Application. This will be confirmed once the proposed layout and extension footprint are fixed, as the depth of the extension and its relationship to the existing rear elevation will determine which route is available.

There is a wish to remain living in the property throughout construction, which will inform the sequencing of the works and the phasing discussions with the contractor.

No site constraints were identified at the initial enquiry stage.
